blinding_guess.why: The code takes GLOBAL_POSITION_INT from the mavlink::standard namespace while the other GPS messages come from mavlink::common, and the packet lists GLOBAL_POSITION_INT under both namespaces, which suggests a namespace move is at issue; whether this revision builds depends on which namespace the paired mavlink release puts that message in, which I did not check.

notes: Package scope is snapshot/mavros (package.xml name mavros, version 2.14.0); the snapshot also holds libmavconn, mavros_extras, mavros_msgs and others, which are separate packages. All seven packet elements are MAVLink C++ API symbols that this package consumes; none is provided, so declares and not_declared are empty. The MAVLink handlers for GPS_RAW_INT, GPS_GLOBAL_ORIGIN, GLOBAL_POSITION_INT and LOCAL_POSITION_NED_SYSTEM_GLOBAL_OFFSET are registered in GlobalPositionPlugin::get_subscriptions (global_position.cpp:149-158, plugin global_position, mavros_plugins.xml:39); SET_GPS_GLOBAL_ORIGIN is built and sent in set_gp_origin_cb (global_position.cpp:544-556). api:mavlink::common::msg::GLOBAL_POSITION_INT is not referenced anywhere in snapshot/mavros: grep for GLOBAL_POSITION finds only the @todo comment at global_position.cpp:297 and mavlink::standard::msg::GLOBAL_POSITION_INT at :301; it therefore has no port and is not in references (it is a consumed element, so it is not put in not_declared either). The same package also uses mavlink::standard for AUTOPILOT_VERSION (sys_status.cpp:823, 851, 1078) and MAV_PROTOCOL_CAPABILITY (mavros_uas.hpp:72, plugin.hpp:40, mission_protocol_base.hpp:52).
